body:
A few thoughts:
- This has the potential of being more cumbersome than a big list on some situations. Even the current showcase in the PR (as of writing this) shows this issue. For some displays, there are not nearly enough Mesh resources to justify it.
- From an user's perspective, the popup appears sometimes, and sometimes not. It's a very frustrating experience. You should be able to show the list, as an option from the originating popup menu.
	- This PR also causes the Quick Load option to be among the list of many available options. This even is more cumbersome than before, especially for Resource types that are more likely to be loaded from disk.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104604 already made it much easier to find and select a desired resource type.

> A few thoughts:
> 
> * This has the potential of being more cumbersome than a big list on some situations. Even the current showcase in the PR (as of writing this) shows this issue. For some displays, there are not nearly enough Mesh resources to justify it.

Thanks for the feedback! Sorry for the confusion, but the threshold was set low (to `10`) for demonstration purposes in the video. By default it's `30`, which afaik would only trigger the dialog for an `@export` of type `Resource` or a custom user type with TONS of children.

I updated the post with a note under the video to highlight this to prevent confusion!

> * From an user's perspective, the popup appears sometimes, and sometimes not. It's a very frustrating experience. You should be able to show the list, as an option from the originating popup menu.

I don't think there are many `Resource` exports that exceed `30`, so unless the user configured it, the dialog would only pop up when there would be an excessive amount of choices for nearly any monitor. 

I did mention having a it also be an option in the original popup menu, but wanted feedback on that first! So I guess that's a yes?

>   * This PR also causes the Quick Load option to be among the list of many available options. This even is more cumbersome than before, especially for Resource types that are more likely to be loaded from disk.

As I also mentioned in the post, clicking the arrow button will always bring up the popup menu, so worse-case scenario you could use the original behavior no matter what! I personally think typing Q, U, I, ENTER would be faster than the scrolling on an excessive popup menu, but that might just be me. 

---

> #104604 already made it much easier to find and select a desired resource type.

This is a great improvement and I was excited to see it implemented! However, at least in my use case, it wouldn't be faster as I have a ton of subclass `Resource`s that start with the same phrase. I'm using `Resource`s to make an eventing system for my game, and the "events" are categorized using a prefix. For example, I have `SetEnable_KillBox`, `SetEnable_TriggerBox`, etc. and `Entity_Move`, `Entity_Rotate`, etc.

My PR supports fuzzy search, and also has the potential to sort fuzzy searches based on match quality, so it would be much easier since I can search "move" or "triggerbox" to get the results I need.

For an example with a built-in Node, that solution doesn't work well with `@export var a: AnimationNode`, as every subclass of `AnimationNode` starts with "AnimationNode". `AnimationNode` in specific is mentioned by one of the proposals I linked in the post as well! (https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3430)

> But I like the functionality of the search though! Can't we somehow merge this dialog with the filtering into the picker? Put a filter box at the top of the picker when there's more than X options?

This is a bit like #114236
